Adams 12 Five Star Schools is deeply committed to a community of excellence, equity, and inclusion in everything we do. We commit to eliminate the predictability of who is included in excellence and who is not. Adams 12 Five Star Schools puts students first and supports our district's mission to elevate student success for every student every day in every classroom.

SUMMARY:
Provide a range of services for students who demonstrate difficulties with learning, academic achievement, social/emotional functioning, and behavior. Serve as a psycho-educational service provider involved in proactive, preventative activities, as well as responding to identified concerns. Provide services based on a combination of problem-solving, consultative, and direct service models.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Develop individual, group or system level interventions which improve identified problems or concerns, including academic, social / emotional / behavioral / mental health needs as they relate to educational progress.
Uses research-based and technically sound practices to drive decision-making and interventions; and collaborates with school personnel and parents in order to develop and modify student intervention strategies.
Facilitates functional assessment of behavior (FBA) and designs/implements and progress monitors intervention plans.
Conducts, interprets and implements student assessment which includes record review, interview, observation, and standardized assessment.
Administers and interprets norm-referenced and curriculum-based edumetric and psychological assessment measures.
Participates in team-based follow-up activities to review student progress, analyze data, and modify individual interventions.
Reviews school-wide assessment data to assist building staff(s) in interpreting and designing school-wide interventions.
Serve as liaison among district building(s), families and community and collaborates with various teams to assure positive outcomes for all learners.
Participate in interdisciplinary staffings to determine the eligibility, appropriate planning, and re-evaluation for students who require special education services/programs.
Comply with Student Support Services and district policies and procedures (e.g., Medicaid billing, accident reporting).
Other duties as assigned.

Education And Related Work Experience

Master's degree or higher.
Must be a minimum of 18 years old.

Criminal background check required for hire.
Must possess, or be able to obtain from, or be in process with, the Colorado Department of Education (CDE) for a valid Colorado Educator License within 30 days of hire.
Must possess the required license and endorsement. Job Title:
Training Coordinator

Job Summary:

The New York City Justice Peer Initiative (JPI) is dedicated to strengthening and expanding opportunities for the Justice Peer workforce. JPI advances this mission through professional-development training, New York State workforce certification, technical assistance for employers, and movement-building and policy efforts that center Justice Peer voices and leadership in transforming the criminal legal and behavioral health treatment systems.

The full-time Training Coordinator is responsible for delivering JPI’s core training curriculum and supporting the continued growth of its workforce-development programs. The C oordinator will conduct at least six trainings per month in locations throughout New York City, Long Island, Westchester County, Upstate New York, and Western New York, helping JPI reach a minimum of 6 00 trainees annually. The Upstate and Western NY training and community engagement will require overnight stays.

The Training Coordinator will also work closely with the Executive Director to plan and coordinate JPI’s annual conference. jobs.description:
Fresh Produce Program | Durham, NC

About The Fresh Produce Program

The Fresh Produce Program (FPP) is a Duke staff- and student-run organization whose mission is to strengthen food security and address nutrition-related health disparities in Durham through produce prescription and food access programs. Our direct-to-door delivery model provides over 600 households experiencing food security with biweekly deliveries of free, fresh, and locally-sourced produce and eggs on Saturday “Distribution Days,” which are complemented by a weekly first-come, first-serve walk-up table for members of the community. Our goal is to help facilitate partnerships between healthcare systems, community organizations, and local food producers and retailers to improve health through nutrition.

Position Summary

FPP seeks a reliable, organized, and community-minded Distribution Day Manager to support our weekly operations of the Fresh Produce Program. This role focuses on coordinating the logistics of produce procurement and distribution, managing relationships with partner organizations, and ensuring that weekly deliveries run smoothly.

The Distribution Day Manager will play a key role in maintaining the program’s weekly distribution workflow—from ordering produce and preparing delivery routes to managing distribution days and coordinating with community partners.

This is a part-time position (approximately 15 hours per week) with standing time commitments on Friday and Saturday mornings.

Compensation: $25/hour

Key Responsibilities

Produce Procurement and Vendor Coordination (approx. 3 hours/week)
Order produce early in the week from program vendors and partners (~1hr)
Pick up produce from the Food Bank of Central and Eastern North Carolina on Fridays at 8:00 AM (~1.5 hr)
Receive and coordinate weekly Friday deliveries from community partner Farmer Foodshare (~1.5 hr)
Distribution Day Operations (approx. 4 hours/week)
Manage and oversee Saturday morning produce distribution logistics
Coordinate volunteers and ensure produce bags are prepared and distributed efficiently
Troubleshoot operational challenges and maintain organized workflow during distribution
Delivery Logistics (approx. 1 hour/week)
Prepare weekly delivery routes and participant lists
Conduct delivery driving as needed (approx. 4 hours/week)
Partner Coordination (approx. 2 hours/week)
Maintain communication with community partners (e.g., MAAME, Molina Healthcare, and other collaborators)
Coordinate scheduling, participation, and collaboration opportunities
Community Engagement (approx. 1 hour/week)
Participate in or support community dinners, gardening activities, and related events Program Development
Participate in periodic program growth and strategy meetings (approx. 1 hour/week)

Qualifications

Required:

Highly organized and able to manage multiple logistical tasks
Comfortable working independently and problem-solving in real time
Strong communication skills and ability to coordinate with multiple partners
Reliable transportation and a valid driver’s license
Ability to lift 25–30 pounds and work in a physically active environment
Comfort working with community members from diverse backgrounds

Preferred

Experience with food access programs, food systems work, or community health initiatives
Prior experience coordinating events, logistics, or distribution operations
Interest in food security, public health, or community-based programs

Why This Role Matters

The Fresh Produce Program provides thousands of pounds of fresh fruits and vegetables to hundreds households experiencing food insecurity each year. The Distribution Day Manager plays a critical role in ensuring that needed food relief reaches participants reliably and that our work remains rooted in the needs of our community.

Our Social Workers make a huge difference to the lives of people across our county, and we remain passionate about investing in retaining our own and developing practice and this an exciting opportunity which offers just that.

undertake section 47 investigations
undertake placement of children into Local Authority care, when it is agreed they can no longer remain at home

examples of creative social work practice to keep children and young people within their families where safe to do so.

The Role

Are you passionate about making a real difference in the lives of children and young people with disabilities and their families?

We are looking for a skilled and committed Social Worker
to join our Children with Disabilities Team
.

In this vital role, you will work directly with children and young people who have a range of additional needs, along with their families, to ensure they receive the right support at the right time. You will complete holistic assessments, plan and coordinate services, and work collaboratively with families and partner agencies to promote positive outcomes and independence. Your work will focus on enabling children to thrive and reach their full potential, with their voice and experience at the centre of everything you do.

We are passionate about providing an inclusive, empowering, and person-centred service. We work closely with families to build trusting relationships, ensuring they feel supported, valued, and part of the process. Our commitment is to help children with disabilities live fulfilling lives, while ensuring their safety, wellbeing, and opportunities to participate in their communities.

Herefordshire is on a journey, and we would like you to be part of our next chapter. This is an exciting opportunity to have a genuine impact on the local authority and to help improve the lives of children and young people with disabilities across the county.

About You

Passionate about supporting children and young people with disabilities and their families to achieve the best possible outcomes
Skilled in assessment, planning, and coordinating multi-agency support, ensuring that each child’s individual needs are fully understood and met
Committed to working collaboratively, inclusively, and creatively with children, families, and professionals from health, education, and social care
Resilient, reflective, and confident in managing complex situations and making child-centred decisions
Able to work effectively within a supportive and specialist team environment, contributing to a culture of learning and continuous improvement
Registered with Social Work England and hold a recognised Social Work qualification (Degree/DipSW/CQSW)
